'''Gemfields Group Ltd''' (formerly Pallinghurst Resources Limited) is a mining company incorporated in [[Guernsey]] and headquartered in [[London]]. It is the 100% owner of Gemfields Limited, specialising in the mining, grading, and sale of coloured gemstones, particularly emeralds and rubies. The group sells rough, uncut gemstones and does not operate any cutting and polishing facilities. The company is the majority owner and the operator of Kagem Mining in [[Zambia]] (emeralds) and Montepuez Ruby Mining in [[Mozambique]] (rubies), which industry sources suggest contribute roughly 25% of global emerald supply and 50% of global ruby supply.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rubies With a Good Heart |url=https://www.cosmopolitan.in/life/features/a17404/rubies-good-heart |website=Cosmopolitan |accessdate=12 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Talking Rubies with Gemfields' Gemologist Elena Basaglia |url=https://www.countryandtownhouse.co.uk/style/jewellery-and-watches/ruby-gemfields-interview/ |website=What's on|date=10 July 2019 |accessdate=12 July 2019}}</ref>

== Gemfields Authorised Auction Partner ==

Gemfields has a special designation for gemstone auction participants who build a track record of winning lots at its auctions. These companies are termed "Gemfields Authorised Auction Partners" and enter into bilateral agreements with Gemfields in relation to that status. Such companies can then use the associated branding & identity in promotional and sales materials.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gemfields Authorised Auction Partner|url=https://www.starlanka.com/gemfields-authorized-auction-partner/|website=starlanka.com|accessdate=12 February 2019}}</ref>

== Mines ==

=== Kagem Mining Limited (Kagem), Zambia ===

* Gemfields holds a 75% stake (remaining 25% held by Zambian government via IDC). 
* Kagem is believed to be the world's single largest producing emerald mine.
* Notable emeralds found in the Kagem deposit include the ‘Inkalamu’, the Lion Emerald, a 5,655 carat Zambian emerald crystal with remarkable clarity and a perfectly balanced golden green hue,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adebayo |first=Bukola |date=2018-10-30 |title=1.1 kg and 5,655 carats: An emerald like no other has been unearthed in Zambia |url=https://www.cnn.com/style/article/massive-emerald-found-in-zambia |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> Chipembele (‘rhino’) which holds the [[Guinness World Records|Guinness World Record]] for largest uncut emerald (World's largest uncut emerald weighs hefty 1.5 kg | Guinness World Records)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-09 |title=‘Horcrux of Voldemort’: World’s largest uncut emerald, weighing 1.5 kg, found in Zambia |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/trending/trending-globally/worlds-largest-uncut-emerald-weighing-1-5-kg-found-in-zambia-8256302/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>, and Imboo (‘buffalo’) (Massive ‘buffalo’ emerald sold in Gemfields auction | News24) at 11,685 carats<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meirovich |first=Leah |date=2025-08-26 |title=Gemfields Recovers Massive 11,685ct. Emerald |url=https://rapaport.com/news/gemfields-mine-recovers-massive-11685ct-emerald-gemstone/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Rapaport |language=en-US}}</ref>. 

=== Montepuez Ruby Mining Limitada (MRM), Mozambique ===

* Gemfields holds a 75% stake (remaining 25% held by Mozambican company Mwiriti Limitada).
* The MRM mine is believed to be situated on one of the most significant recently discovered ruby deposits in the world.
* Notable rubies found at MRM include the Rhino Ruby (40.23 carats),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ruby dubbed the ‘Rhino’ sells for undisclosed sum |url=https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/8729-ruby-dubbed-the-rhino-sells-for-undisclosed-sum |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=nationaljeweler.com |language=en}}</ref> and the Eyes of the Dragon (45 carats).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thai gem company buys Gemfields’ matching rubies |url=https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/8786-thai-gem-company-buys-gemfields-matching-rubies |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=nationaljeweler.com |language=en}}</ref>
* MRM is constructing a second processing plant (PP2), which is expected to triple the mine's rough ruby processing capacity and estimated to begin operations in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Haripersad |first=Devina |title=Ruby miner nears completion of production-tripling plant |url=https://www.miningweekly.com/article/ruby-miner-nears-completion-of-production-tripling-plant-2025-06-06 |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Mining Weekly |language=en}}</ref>
* Multiple news reports explain how the mine's location and it's rich ruby deposit have attracted smuggling syndicates to the region. This has resulted in several violent incursions on the MRM concession.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Hard Time for Gemfields in Mozambique |url=https://rapaport.com/magazine-article/a-hard-time-for-gemfields-in-mozambique/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Rapaport |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Subsidiaries==

===Fabergé===

* Gemfields Group Limited (then Pallinghurst Resources Limited) bought up the Fabergé trademarks, licenses and associated rights related to the name in 2007, reversing the fragmentation of the brand over the past 90 years, and reinstated connections with the Fabergé family;
* Gemfields Limited acquired 100% stake in Fabergé in January 2013, enabling high-profile marketing of coloured gemstones;
** Fabergé Completes Merger with Colored Gemstone Company<ref>{{Cite news |last=DeMarco |first=Anthony |title=Fabergé Completes Merger with Colored Gemstone Company |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/anthonydemarco/2013/01/30/faberge-completes-merger-with-colored-gemstone-company/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>
** Gemfields buys Fabergé to create gem champion<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cordeiro |first=Brenton |date=2012-11-22 |title=Gemfields buys Fabergé to create gem champion |url=https://www.timescolonist.com/business/gemfields-buys-faberge-to-create-gem-champion-4556049 |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Times Colonist |language=en}}</ref>
* Gemfields Limited sold 100% stake in Fabergé amid Group-wide cash constraints, in order to focus portfolio on the mining of coloured gemstones
** Gemfields considers selling Fabergé as it cuts costs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Correspondent |first=Jessica Newman, Leisure Industries |date=2024-12-24 |title=Gemfields considers selling Fabergé as it cuts costs |url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/gemfields-considers-selling-faberge-as-it-cuts-costs-qllk86vct |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}}</ref>
** Gemfields sells Fabergé for $50m to focus on rubies and emeralds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Correspondent |first=Helen Cahill, M&A and Restructuring |date=2025-08-11 |title=Gemfields sells Fabergé for $50m to focus on rubies and emeralds |url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/gemfields-sells-faberge-for-50-million-to-focus-on-rubies-and-emeralds-xvnxqkgf9 |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Corporate governance ==

* Chairman: Bruce Cleaver (formerly CEO at De Beers)
** [https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/gemfields-bruce-cleaver-were-like-de-beers-was-30-years-ago-sxxwxftlt?msockid=3edf868ad2036a4606169387d39c6b30 Gemfields’ Bruce Cleaver: ‘We’re like De Beers was 30 years ago’]
* CEO: Sean Gilbertson.
* CFO: David Lovett.
* Non-Executive Directors: Bruce Cleaver (Chair); Kieran Daly; Kwape Mmela; Mary Reilly; Patrick Sacco; Simon Scott; Louis du Preez
* Major shareholders: Assore International Holdings (approximately 26-29%), Rational Expectations, Oasis.

== Sustainability and responsibility ==

* Committed to responsible mining, undertaking independent third party audits, attainting International Standards Organization (ISO) certification at operations, and committing MRM to undertake the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance (IRMA)<ref>{{Cite web |last=IRMA |date=2025-06-10 |title=Gemfields commits Montepuez Ruby Mining to IRMA audit |url=https://responsiblemining.net/2025/06/10/gemfields-commits-montepuez-ruby-mining-to-irma-audit/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=IRMA - The Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance |language=en-US}}</ref>
* Support education, healthcare and livelihood projects near their mine locations.
* Implements backfilling and environmental rehabilitation at mining sites.
* Gemfields Foundation is the charitable arm of Gemfields, through which donors can contribute funding to directly support community and conservation projects in Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gemfields Foundation |url=https://www.gemfieldsfoundation.org/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=www.gemfieldsfoundation.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Legal and regulatory developments ==

* Anti-Bribery Case in Madagascar: In mid 2024, Romy Andrianarisoa, ex-chief of staff to Madagascar's president, and associate Philippe Tabuteau were convicted in London for attempting to solicit approximately CHF 270,000 (≈USD 300,000) plus a 5% equity stake from Gemfields in exchange for a sapphire mining license. The pair were arrested in 2023 after Gemfields reported the approach to the UK National Crime Agency. Andrianarisoa received a 3.5-year sentence; Tabuteau received 2 years 3 months. First-ever foreign public official convicted under the UK's Bribery Act 2010. 
** Madagascan presidential aide charged with seeking £225,000 bribe in UK<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-14 |title=Madagascan presidential aide charged with seeking £225,000 bribe in UK |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-66496985 |access-date=2025-11-16 |language=en-GB}}</ref>
** The former chief of staff to the Malagasy president, prosecuted in London, was found guilty of corruption.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-02-21 |title=Poursuivie à Londres, l’ex-directrice de cabinet du président malgache reconnue coupable de corruption |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/afrique/article/2024/02/21/poursuivie-a-londres-l-ex-directrice-de-cabinet-du-president-malgache-reconnue-coupable-de-corruption_6217675_3212.html |access-date=2025-11-16 |language=fr}}</ref>

== Controversies ==

* 2019 Human Rights Settlement: Agreed, on a no-admission-of-liability basis, the settlement of all claims brought by an English law firm on behalf of individuals living in the vicinity of MRM's mining concession. The settlement figure was GBP 5.8 million comprising the sum to be distributed to the claimants and legal expenses of the law firm acting on their behalf.
* 2024 Anti-Bribery Scandal: As detailed above.
* 2024–25 Market Challenges: Strategic cost-cutting has drawn investor attention; share price dropped approximately 50%. 
** Gemfields shares slide as it addresses market challenges - Sharecast.com<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gemfields shares slide as it addresses market challenges |url=https://www.sharecast.com/news/aim-bulletin/gemfields-shares-slide-as-it-addresses-market-challenges--18370216.html |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Sharecast |language=en}}</ref>
** Gemfields Suspends Emerald Mining Amid Market Pressures and Focuses on Ruby Growth<ref>{{Cite web |last=service |first=diamond world news |date=2024-12-25 |title=Gemfields Suspends Emerald Mining Amid Market Pressures and Focuses on Ruby Growth |url=https://www.diamondworld.net/news/gemfields-suspends-emerald-mining-amid-market-pressures-and-focuses-on-ruby-growth |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Diamond World |language=en}}</ref>
** Gemfields to Halt Some Operations and Sell Businesses<ref>{{Cite web |last=Billen |first=Hugo |date=2024-12-23 |title=Gemfields to Halt Some Operations, Sell Businesses Amid Market Woes |url=https://rapaport.com/news/gemfields-to-halt-some-operations-sell-businesses-amid-market-woes/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=Rapaport |language=en-US}}</ref>
